title: PicardExternalCoefficientsAffineCechComparison
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], f:X -> Spec(k), g:Y -> Spec(k) scheme morphisms [def-pc-scheme], and F,G quasi-coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Let I be finite and U:I -> Opens(X) an open family covering top with every nonempty finite intersection affine. Let V be an affine open of Y and q a nonnegative integer. Form C by restricting the native Cech complex Cech(U,F) [def-sc-module-cech-comparison] from Gamma(X,O) to k along scalarMap f top. Put N=scalarObj(V.ι composed with g)(G|V)(top). There is an isomorphism of additive groups from H^q(pr2 inverse V,externalCupCoefficients f g F G) [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] to the underlying additive group of the degree-q homology of the termwise tensorRight(N) complex of C. This does not identify homology of C with scalarCohomology or commute tensor with homology.

source.place: Lemma 33.29.1 (varieties-lemma-kunneth), affine-open paragraph and equality of Cech complexes after Let V be an affine open; checked online 2026-10-13

proof.text: For an arbitrary quasi-coherent module on an affine-intersection cover, beta of the injective-resolution Cech double complex is a quasi-isomorphism. Alpha induces an isomorphism when the family covers top. Compose H(beta), inverse H(alpha), and the inverse resolution cohomology comparison to obtain the native module-valued Cech-to-global-cohomology isomorphism.

Put W=pr2 inverse V and U_i'=W.ι inverse(pr1 inverse U_i). Finite inverse image commutes with the finite intersections (proved by underlying sets); image along W.ι of each intersection is pr1 inverse U_intersection intersect pr2 inverse V. This is affine by the affine fibre-product formula, using the proved isAffineOpen_preimage_inf_preimage_pullback. Image under an open immersion reflects affine opens. Inverse image commutes with iSup and sends top to top, so U' covers W. Quasi-coherence of the external coefficient follows from quasi-coherence of pullback and of tensor. For tensorPullback, transport the ordinary pullback result along the unique isomorphism of left adjoints.

Apply the open-restriction module cohomology isomorphism to W, followed by the inverse native Cech comparison from step 1 after forgetting scalars. Exact scalar forgetting commutes with homology by ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso. Apply homology to the geometric complex isomorphism, then use exact scalar forgetting again to identify this with the underlying additive group of the tensor complex homology. Every arrow in this composite is an isomorphism, giving the claimed Nonempty witness.

lean.statement:
theorem picardExternalCupCoefficients_affine_cech_comparison
    (k : Type w) [Field k] (X Y : Scheme.{w})
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [G.IsQuasicoherent]
    {ι : Type w} [Finite ι] (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ (n : ℕ) (y : Fin (n + 1) → ι), IsAffineOpen (⨅ l, U (y l)))
    (hcover : iSup U = ⊤) (V : Y.Opens) (hV : IsAffineOpen V) (q : ℕ) :
    let R := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (scalarMap f ⊤)
    let C := (R.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj
      ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat)
    let T := tensorRight (scalarObj (V.ι ≫ g) (G.restrict V.ι) (Opposite.op ⊤))
    Nonempty
      (((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace q
        ((pullback.snd f g) ⁻¹ᵁ V)).obj (externalCupCoefficients f g F G)) ≅
        (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{w} k) AddCommGrpCat.{w}).obj
          (((T.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℕ)).obj C).homology q))
